subject: SLA: burst tolerance and monthly credit smoothing
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Martin <sophie@finapp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed approach: burst tolerance + monthly credit smoothing

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for the detailed call this morning. Per our conversation, I wanted to put a concrete starting point on the SLA language and a pragmatic exception path for the burst/batched inference patterns you highlighted. Attached is a redline of the SLA (redwood-sla-draft_v2.pdf) and a short excerpt from our operational playbook showing how we measure and attribute availability (ops-playbook-excerpt.txt).

High-level proposal:
- Baseline uptime guarantee: 99.9% for Redwood hosted inference (standard tier).
- Dedicated/Reserved pools: 99.95% uptime when customer reserves dedicated capacity (separate amendment).
- Monthly credit calculation: tiered % of monthly invoice based on downtime bands (we provided the table in the PDF).
- Burst/batched inference carveout: temporary, short-lived spikes caused by short windows of pooled batching or queue saturation will be smoothed using a 30-day rolling window before crediting is triggered. The idea is to avoid penalizing transient cloud load spikes while still protecting you from systemic regressions.
- Maintenance carveouts: scheduled maintenance >48 hours notice; emergency maintenance documented in postmortem; these are excluded from remedy calculations per usual.

We think the 30-day smoothing achieves two goals: it prevents credits for single-sub-minute blips while keeping a short enough window to surface real regressions quickly. That said, we are open to a 60- or 90-day smoothing if you need a longer runway for seasonal variability — we can model both.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm whether FinApp can accept 99.9% hosted baseline with the 30-day smoothing exception.
2) If you need 99.95 for production-critical workloads, we can expedite a Dedicated addendum with a committed pool and a different credit ladder.
3) Ben/Marissa will follow up with exact credit caps (monthly max as a % of invoice) and a DocuSign link for the amendment.

Please review the attached redline and call out any required definitions (e.g., how you measure "unavailable" for batched jobs). I can loop in Kimberly from Legal if you want us to take a first pass on tighter definition language.

Thanks —
Soojin

From: Sophie Martin <sophie@finapp.com>

Cc: FinApp Legal <legal@finapp.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed approach: burst tolerance + monthly credit smoothing

Soojin —

Appreciate the write-up and attachments. Quick thoughts from the FinApp product team:

- Baseline: our bar for production is 99.95% (customer-facing latency-sensitive flows). 99.9% would be a step backward for those routes.
- We like the idea of smoothing for burst noise, but 30 days feels short if you're using rolling averages on per-minute windows — we see multi-week seasonality with batch jobs. Would you share the model showing how credits would trigger on a sample month with a 30-, 60-, and 90-day smooth?
- Regarding dedicated: yes, a dedicated pool could be an acceptable path — but we need to understand lead times, cost bump, and rollback behavior if utilization is low.
- Credits cap: we can accept a monthly cap, but the cap should be meaningful — e.g., not less than 20% of the affected route's monthly spend in the severe bands.

FinApp Legal will weigh in on the definitions and maintenance carveouts. For now, please send the modeled scenarios (30/60/90-day smoothing) and the proposed monthly cap table.

Thanks —
Sophie
Sophie Martin
Head of Product, FinApp
sophie@finapp.com

Subject: Re: Proposed approach: burst tolerance + monthly credit smoothing

Sophie —

Thanks for the quick feedback. I've attached a short spreadsheet (included inline in the PDF) that shows sample months with synthetic spike patterns and how the credit triggers under 30/60/90-day smoothing. High-level takeaways:
- 30-day smoothing is the most responsive: single-week incidents will show as a bump but only generate credits if they materially depress the rolling availability.
- 60/90-day smoothing dampens credits across months; useful if your workload has predictable monthly seasonality.

Proposed compromise to align with your 99.95 ask without fully committing to Dedicated today:
- Offer a "Production SLA Pilot": for three months we can apply 99.95 to the three mission-critical routes you specify, but with a slightly higher credits cap (to balance cost and risk). During the pilot we'd monitor hit rates and see if a Dedicated pool is warranted.
- If after the pilot the routes meet utilization and reliability thresholds, we can convert to a Dedicated commitment with the 99.95 guaranteed and a lower credit cap.

Credit caps (example banding):
- Severe (>1% monthly downtime): 30% of route spend
- Major (0.5% - 1%): 15% of route spend
- Minor (<0.5%): 5% of route spend
Monthly aggregate cap: 40% of route spend (negotiable for enterprise).

I'll draft a short amendment text for the pilot and the smoothing options and share a DocuSign link once Sophie confirms the pilot routes.

Cheers —
Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Team —

We reviewed the redline and have a few requested clarifications before we can accept any pilot or amendment:
1) Precise metric definition: we require the SLA to define "unavailable" at the API-route level (per 5-minute bucket) and to state clearly whether client-side timeouts contribute to counted unavailability.
2) Aggregation: the smoothing window must be explicitly defined (we prefer 60 days for our business reporting). Please show the formula you use to compute the rolling availability number.
3) Maintenance: we need a guaranteed minimum notice of 72 hours for scheduled maintenance affecting production routes. Emergency maintenance should include a postmortem within 7 business days.

We also asked our ops team to review the playbook excerpt; they want a clarifying sentence about how you attribute multi-tenant outages vs. routing/config issues specific to FinApp. If you can update the redline addressing these three items, we can fast-track internal approval.

Regards —
FinApp Legal
legal@finapp.com

Subject: Re: Proposed approach: burst tolerance + monthly credit smoothing — action items and next steps

Sophie / Legal team —

Thanks for the clear ask. Summary of what we'll update and how we propose to proceed:

1) Metric definition: we'll add a per-route 5-minute-bucket availability definition and explicitly state that client-side timeouts (HTTP 5xx from Redwood) are counted; network-level client timeouts will be excluded unless they correlate with server-side errors.

2) Smoothing window: we can accept 60-day smoothing language as FinApp Legal requested. For the Production SLA Pilot we propose to start reporting with both 30- and 60-day numbers so you can see responsiveness vs. stability; the formal remedy will use 60-day smoothing.

3) Maintenance notice: we'll move to 72 hours minimum for scheduled maintenance affecting routes you designate as production-critical. Emergency maintenance postmortems committed within 5 business days (we can push to 7 if you require it; Marissa, can you confirm internal SLA on postmortems?).

4) Pilot offer: we will provision a trial dedicated pool for the three routes you nominate. During the 3-month pilot:
   - We will measure route-level availability with the agreed definitions.
   - Remedy ladder: use the credit banding Ben proposed, but reduce the Monthly aggregate cap to 35% of route spend for the pilot.

5) Next administrative steps:
   - I'll upload an updated redline to the shared Drive link (https://drive.redwood.com/shared/finapp/sla-v2) and publish a DocuSign amendment link (https://redwood.app/docusign/DA-987654-amendment).
   - Once Sophie confirms the three pilot routes, Ben/ops will schedule provisioning and Marissa will own the postmortem SLA timeline.

If this looks ok to FinApp, I'll send the DocuSign package tomorrow morning. We are aligned to get the pilot started quickly and measure results.

Thanks —
Soojin
